_note:
The SAME FLOOR as cold-storage-draught, and a completely different operation. The squad walks in with the map already learned and every instinct wrong: the imager reads nothing, the breakers do not matter, and the aisles they used as fencing lanes last time are now sightlines they have to hold. GDD 15.2 calls this epistemic and operational variation; this is what it looks like when the map is a constant and the incident is the variable.

It starts in Aisle B, at the far end, because the supervisor's statement says so and because the aisle is a long straight run — a single camera at the south end holds the whole lane, and that is the discovery the procedure turns on.
_variationNote:
GDD §14.4. The figure is the one incident where the ORIGIN carries most of the variation: the whole operation is a sightline problem, and which end of which aisle it is standing in decides whether one camera holds it or three do. The four origins are the four aisle ends.

⚠ NO ROUTES ARE ON THE LIST. Aisle B is the operation; jamming a door that changes which way a squad walks into it is variation, and jamming one that walls the aisle off is an unwinnable state. Neither door on this floor can be shut without risking the second, so this incident varies in everything except geometry.

`camera-still` and `thermal-null` are NOT droppable. Both are instrument-gated and both are a rules path that cannot be replaced by walking somewhere — dropping one would leave a squad who spent cargo on the instrument with nothing to point it at.

briefing.headline: Repeat sighting, cold storage aisle B
briefing.report: The night supervisor called in 'a man standing at the end of aisle B' four times in one shift, walked the aisle four times, and found nothing. On the fifth she watched the camera instead and it stayed. That was eleven days ago.

known.text: The supervisor is at the stair head and will give a statement.
Site electrical log shows fourteen unexplained brownouts on the storage circuit.
A night-shift name stopped signing in eleven days ago and was not reported absent.

_placementNote:
⚠ TWO WAYS A COORDINATE BREAKS A FLOOR, AND THIS INCIDENT HAD BOTH.

`contextAction` is nearest-wins and `sourceInReach` returns the FIRST hit in this array rather than the nearest, over a probe of `reachMetres + 0.6` = 2.8m. So a source inside 2.8m of another source answers for it; and a source inside 2.8m of where an operative stands to work a breaker or a door beats the fixture outright, because it is nearer. The second kind costs the whole operation — see the note in cold-storage-draught.json, where a charging rack 2.7m from the office breaker took the breaker's verb away and the containment bot never got into the office.

The rule applied here: every source added or moved at revision 0.2.0 is more than `reach + probe` = 5.0m from every door centre and every circuit switch, so it cannot be a candidate at any point from which the fixture is in reach; and no two sources are inside 2.8m of each other.

Two pairs were already inside the source-to-source radius, and both were broken before anybody stood on them:
  · `thermal-null` was at [-0.5, 6.0], 2.40m from `dust-ring`. Standing on the sighting offered 'Examine the floor'; after the ring was logged it offered nothing at all. Moved to [-0.5, 5.0].
  · `night-shift-roster` was at [-10.4, -9.2], 2.34m from `brownout-log` on the same desk, in an office 3.8m square that also holds the storage breaker and a door — three interactables it cannot carry. Moved out to the clock-in board at the stair head, [11.2, -11.4], which is where a shift roster hangs anyway and where the squad walks past it on the way in.

Aisle B now reads as a line down the lane — the ring at the far end, the sighting, the drag marks, the camera position at the mouth — spaced 3.4m, 3.4m and 4.6m. That is the aisle telling the story in the order you walk it, and every step of it is clear of the next.
